issues.legal_issue: Withdrawing an earlier request to stay court proceedings under the former arbitration regime does not, by itself, bar a party from seeking a reference to arbitration under the later regime or create an estoppel against that request.
material_facts: A civil suit sought dissolution of a partnership and accounts, and the partnership agreement contained an arbitration clause.
The defendants had obtained a stay of the suit under the former arbitration regime, but later withdrew that application after the former regime was repealed.
The defendants subsequently sought a reference to arbitration under the later regime, and the High Court rejected the request on the basis of the withdrawal and estoppel.
issues.conclusion: The earlier withdrawal created no legal impediment to invoking the later regime, and estoppel could not deprive the defendants of the right to seek a reference to arbitration. The matter was remitted for consideration under the later regime.
issues.legal_principle: The former regime’s provision for staying court proceedings and the later regime’s provision for referring parties to arbitration serve distinct purposes. Under Section 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, a judicial authority must refer the parties to arbitration where an action concerns a matter covered by an arbitration agreement and a party applies no later than its first statement on the substance of the dispute. The later regime does not require a separate stay of court proceedings, and Section 8(3) permits arbitration to commence or continue, and an award to be made, while the court action or reference application is pending. The former application’s withdrawal did not prevent recourse to the later regime. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.civil_action_concerns_arbitrable_dispute: A party brought a civil action concerning a dispute covered by an arbitration agreement.
predicates.party_seeks_arbitration_under_new_framew: A party asked the court to refer the dispute to arbitration under the later arbitration framework.
predicates.prior_stay_application_withdrawn_after_r: A party withdrew an earlier request to stay the civil action after the former arbitration framework had been repealed.

issues.definition: When a civil action concerns an arbitrable dispute, a party seeks arbitration under the later framework, and an earlier stay request was withdrawn after repeal, that withdrawal does not bar the arbitration reference request.

issues.legal_issue: A decision on a receiver or sales restriction in an ongoing partnership business must account for the competing parties’ interests and the effects of disrupting the business, including whether a party-managed arrangement under court control is feasible.
material_facts: The dispute concerned dissolution of a partnership and accounts, and the partnership agreement contained an arbitration clause.
The business involved ongoing construction and sales, with substantial funds said to have been invested in the work.
The plaintiff’s husband had contributed the land, while construction was said to have been funded by other partners or the builders.

The High Court favoured appointing a receiver and prohibiting sales without considering the effect on the firm’s business or the feasibility of a party receiver operating under strict court control and accountability.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s and Trial Court’s orders and remitted the matter for fresh consideration of the parties’ claims and rights under the later arbitration regime. The existing status quo was to continue until the Trial Court made new directions.
issues.legal_principle: A court considering a receiver or injunction must balance the interests of both sides and consider the impact of freezing a continuing business. It should consider whether a party receiver could manage day-to-day business subject to effective court control and accountability before imposing a third-party receivership and a complete prohibition on sales. Where an arbitration clause exists, recourse to the civil court for adjudication or orders of this kind without an intention to pursue arbitration may not arise. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.arbitration_linked_partnership_dispute: The proceeding concerned a partnership dispute covered by an arbitration agreement.
predicates.court_ordered_receiver_or_sales_restrict: A court ordered a receiver or restricted sales of partnership assets.
predicates.ongoing_business_threatened_by_freeze: The proposed restrictions threatened to disrupt the partnership’s continuing business activities.
predicates.competing_interests_or_party_receiver_op: The court did not assess the parties’ competing interests or the feasibility of a party-managed arrangement under court control.

issues.definition: When an arbitration-linked partnership dispute involves a receiver or sales restriction that threatens an ongoing business, and the court has not assessed competing interests or a party-managed alternative, the interim order is set aside for fresh balanced determination.
